problem: Existing object navigation methods each inject a single inductive bias (association, memory, SLAM, deadlock module) into one black-box network, so only some navigation abilities are learned well. With sparse and ambiguous rewards, one thinking stream cannot implicitly decouple all needed abilities, and enhancing one can hurt others.
motivation: Object navigation needs several distinct abilities (searching, navigating to a seen target, exploring, avoiding obstacles), but the field has no unified inductive-bias paradigm. The authors observe that decoupling abilities by input, encoding and reward could unify prior methods, while keeping end-to-end training and adding interpretability.
key_idea: Decouple object navigation into five meta-abilities (intuition, search, navigation, exploration, obstacle), each with its own specialized input, lightweight encoder and auxiliary reward, and fuse them with a squeeze-excitation-style collaboration module before an LSTM A3C policy.
insight: Giving each meta-ability a dedicated input, encoder and reward makes each inductive bias more effective: MT's search thinking is stronger than DOA's (SSR 97.76 vs 95.82) even though it uses a simplified DOA attention. Adding thinkings raises SR steadily (43.48 with intuition only, then 75.94 with search, 79.62 with navigation, 81.97 with exploration, 83.14 with obstacle). The meta-ability reward helps only in early training: using it for all episodes drops SR to 81.31. DOA improves search but worsens exploration (REP 7.14 vs baseline 5.28), showing that undecoupled improvements trade off against other abilities.
method: Meta-Ability Decoupling (MAD) paradigm: five stages: pick meta-abilities, choose inputs, design encoders, design collaboration, design rewards; decoupling happens in input, encoding and reward while staying end-to-end.

Thinking inputs: intuition uses ResNet18 7x7x512 features; search uses DETR object features (N x 262); navigation uses the target-oriented memory graph of target-visible nodes; exploration uses historical positions and angles; obstacle uses positions of known unreachable nodes.

Thinking encoders: intuition uses a pointwise conv; search uses DOA object attention weights for the target; navigation uses TAMSA (egocentric transform, multi-scale TCN, target-index channel recalibration); exploration and obstacle use polar coordinates, FC layers and average pooling.
MTC module: concatenates and squeezes all thinking outputs into a holistic feature Z, then generates sigmoid channel excitations that recalibrate each thinking.
Policy: layer-normed concatenation, then an LSTM policy trained with A3C.

Meta-ability reward: adds small +/-0.01 rewards for search, navigation, exploration (repeated states) and obstacle (collision) on top of the base reward (-0.01 per step, +0.01 for MoveAhead, +5 on success). It is used only for the first 0.2M of 3M training episodes.
MT-ZS: replaces one-hot target encoding and the fixed attention matrix with GloVe cosine similarity to the target, for zero-shot object navigation.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 (frozen) + DETR features + small thinking encoders + LSTM, trained from scratch with A3C
setting.training_data: AI2-Thor (20 rooms per scene type for training) and RoboTHOR (60 apartments), 3M navigation episodes with RL, 18 workers on 2 RTX 2080Ti; no extra data
setting.observation: single-view egocentric RGB, plus agent pose (position and angle) history and detector outputs
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead, RotateLeft, RotateRight, LookDown, LookUp, Done
setting.privileged: Agent coordinates/poses are used for memory graphs; unreachable nodes and target-visible nodes are recorded during navigation (no GT map is used)

numbers.extra: success threshold 1.5 m; ALL targets; L>=5 also reported

The benchmarks are AI2-Thor/RoboTHOR (not in the canonical list). The splits are test (AI2-Thor) and val (RoboTHOR), inferred from the setup text.
results: MT beats the best previous end-to-end method DOA by 8.82 SR and 9.96 SPL on AI2-Thor (83.14/50.23 vs 74.32/40.27) and by about 6.6 SR / 7 SPL on RoboTHOR. On zero-shot navigation, MT-ZS beats ZSON on unseen classes (68.61 vs 57.32 SR on the 18/4 split; 62.40 vs 52.74 on 14/8).
limitations: The meta-abilities are chosen from human experience, and more abstract ones cannot be decoupled automatically.
Evaluated only on object navigation in AI2-Thor/RoboTHOR simulation, with no real robot and no Habitat/HM3D benchmarks.
The gain is smaller in simple scenes such as the kitchen and bathroom; the paper also reports a lower NSNPL than SLAM methods, and inconsistent numbers between tables.
